newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB eyeing Pakistan's June 25 white wheat tender.
newsitem.headline: CWB eyeing Pakistan's June 25 white wheat tender.

text.p: The Canadian Wheat Board on Thursday said it was "interested" in Pakistan's June 25 tender for 500,000 tonnes of optional origin white wheat.

"Yes, we're interested in Pakistan's tender," said Jim Pietryk, a CWB spokesman. "Sales is not going to offer on a tender if they don't think they can cover it. You've got to keep these customers happy."
The CWB said on Tuesday said it would accept 40 percent of its delivery calls for all grades of Canada Prairie Spring White (CPSW) wheat for the final quarter of the 1996/97 (Aug/July) crop year.
A Pakistani embassy spokesman in Washington on Thursday said the white wheat would likely be sourced either from Canada, the United States or Australia for July 11 to August 10 shipment.

The CWB said in March it had to defer 1.5 million tonnes in wheat sales to the 1997/98 crop year due to a severe backlog in ocean vessels at Canada's Pacific ports that cost it at least C$15 million in demurrage fines.
"The ability to deliver will be a factor, but they (CWB sales) make that determination because you have to be able to deliver on what you offer," Pietryk added.
